assessment: The incumbent is plausibly adequate when course assignments remain stable: those 24 files had seven-minute median handling. Overall, however, 32/40 intended course sets and 17-minute median handling miss the targets. Assignment changes coincide with six affected exports, supporting investigation of week selection without establishing causality. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Short job runtimes and long replacement waits suggest additional service-process delay, but elapsed waiting is not measured coordinator handling. Zero observed cross-center rows is bounded evidence; the split-course center was absent.

openings.claim: Using present course metadata for a requested week may make exports sensitive to later assignment or naming changes, creating omissions or apparent omissions.
openings.delta: Test whether the incumbent preserves historical course identity and membership across metadata changes; distinguish missing records from labels coordinators cannot match.
openings.prediction: For fixed attendance and a fixed requested week, assignment or name changes alter exported membership or matching success; an unchanged control does not.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, vary assignment and rename separately, compare participant/course membership and coordinator matching before and after, and include the omitted split-course condition plus another center. Keep the documented CSV and attendance entry active. Stop any proposed repair at the six-day and hosting limits.
assumptions: Staging can reproduce these metadata changes.
Historical reconstruction availability and repair effort remain unknown.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling primarily come from course-set reconciliation, or from download/import and replacement-request steps?
openings.delta: Locate the measured handling burden separately from replacement waiting before choosing the first change.
openings.prediction: A reconciliation bottleneck produces concentrated checking/correction time; a transfer or request bottleneck produces concentrated time in those steps, even with a correct course set.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions with fabricated correct and affected CSVs. Time checking, correcting, downloading, importing, and requesting separately; record waiting separately. Retain only timing and issue categories within the private service or authorized workspace.
assumptions: Six coordinators cannot establish the next-40-export success rate.
